title: 2026-06-27 QBR - Borealis Systems - Health Check
summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage trends, cost drivers, recent reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment for next quarter. Borealis is seeing steady query growth (10-12% mo/mo) but token spend outpacing predictions due to expanded agent workflows. Team discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs and requested updated cost scenarios and a performance benchmark on p95 latency. Action items include Redwood sharing detailed per-route cost breakdown, scheduling a SE-led technical deep dive for private deployment options, and CSM follow-up on rolling out recommended batching settings.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-27
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Kim (Redwood CSM); Maya Ortiz (Head of ML Ops, Borealis), Ethan Blake (Platform Eng), Lina Chen (CTO)

Summary (auto): Quick QBR focusing on usage growth, unexpected cost drivers, a recent reliability spike, and upcoming roadmap priorities.

[00:00] Jordan: All right everyone, thanks for joining — really appreciate you carving out time for the QBR. we wanted to run through usage, costs, reliability, and next quarter roadmap. how's everyone doing?
[00:15] Maya: doing good, thanks. busy ramping a few agent workflows. had a couple outages last month which is why we wanted to sync.
[00:25] Jordan: Yes saw the incident notes — Sam can you give the brief incident recap?
[00:30] Sam: yeah so on 6/10 we observed a p95 latency spike across a handful of routes, roughly 3x baseline for about 28 minutes, root cause appears to be a bad cache invalidation event combined with increased concurrent prefixes during a marketing burst, logs show fallback to a larger model variant which drove token cost up as well.
[01:05] Priya: to add — the KV cache eviction threshold was hit because of an atypical prefix distribution; the runtime routed to the fallback variant per our policy. we rolled the rule back and performance normalized.
[01:30] Ethan: ok that matches what we saw on our side; costs jumped that day as well which triggered alerts. we budgeted for steady growth but that burst pushed us over forecast.
[01:50] Lina: can you remind us of the fallback policy? is it possible to prefer throttling over variant fallback?
[02:05] Priya: great question. current policy is latency-first for our enterprise tier which prefers model variant fallback to keep end-user latency under SLOs. we can change routing policy to cost-first or introduce a hybrid where we fail requests or queue if capacity constrained — depends on business tolerance.
[02:40] Jordan: that's an important tradeoff — may be worth a canary for cost-sensitive routes. Maya, what are your key success criteria for the next quarter?
[02:55] Maya: A few things — keep p95 under 600ms for core chat flows, reduce token spend by 15% without hurting quality, and get the private deployment POC scoped so we can test residency and KMS integration.
[03:20] Jordan: good, that's actionable. On the cost side, we've been looking at batching and quantization, also per-route caching. Priya can share some suggested settings.
[03:35] Priya: yes; initial pass suggests enabling continuous batching on routes with short-turn conversations, prefix cache TTL tweaks, and a per-route max-batch window of 40ms for conversational routes. also recommend exploring 4-bit quantized variants for non-creative outputs.
[04:05] Ethan: curious what the expected quality delta is on 4-bit for our summarization tasks?
[04:18] Priya: tests vary by model — in our benchmarks for similar workloads we saw negligible regression for extractive summarization but some drop on open-ended generation; we should run a quick eval on your prompt set.
[04:40] Maya: we'll share a corpus of representative prompts.
[04:45] Jordan: perfect. on Dedicated vs Hosted, Lina flagged concerns about compliance and data residency — can we recap the Private deployment options?
[04:58] Priya: Private options: VPC-hosted private control plane, or fully on-prem with air-gapped package. both support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logging. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools but still managed by Redwood; private gives you more network control.
[05:20] Lina: for us the main blocker is KMS and audit logs retention policy — do you support customer-managed keys and 12 month audit retention?
[05:35] Sam: yes, we can integrate with customer-managed KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) and extend audit retention with our enterprise add-on; we'll include specifics in the security pack.
[05:50] Ethan: estimate for Dedicated sizing — we need sustained throughput for 1M tokens/day with p95 under 700ms, any back-of-envelope numbers?
[06:05] Priya: rough estimate: for your model mix and request profile, a 4-GPU dedicated pool (A100/80GB class equivalent) with autoscale headroom should hit that. we'll produce a detailed sizing doc.
[06:20] Jordan: i'll put together a pricing scenarios doc for hosted vs dedicated vs private — include cost per million tokens and committed discount tiers.
[06:30] Maya: great. on reliability, can we add a healthcheck that alerts earlier when prefix distribution skews? maybe tie into our existing monitoring.
[06:45] Priya: yes we can surface prefix entropy metrics and set adaptive TTLs; we also have hooks for Prometheus and PagerDuty integration.
[07:05] Ethan: another ask — can we get per-route token breakout in the dashboard? current dashboard is aggregated and it's hard to tie costs to features.
[07:20] Sam: that's on our roadmap — Priya, do we have an ETA to export per-route cost CSV?
[07:30] Priya: I can export a per-route spreadsheet from our usage logs and share this week, we'll also propose a self-serve dashboard ETA in the roadmap doc.
[07:40] Lina: one more security question — SOC2 status and recent penetration test?
[07:50] Sam: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant; we completed a third-party pentest in Q1 2026 — details and remediations will be in the security pack.
[08:05] Jordan: switching to roadmap — Borealis roadmap items and timelines? Maya?
[08:10] Maya: Q3 we plan to enable multi-agent orchestrations and expand to 3 additional product features that will increase inference volume. we wanted to understand model upgrade impacts and how Redwood handles model rollouts.
[08:30] Priya: rollouts support canary and A/B policies, automatic fallback to previous model if regression detected, and pinning of model versions per route. we'll propose a rollout plan to minimize regression risk.
[08:50] Ethan: would appreciate a dry-run plan for canary with traffic percentages we should use.
[09:00] Priya: standard is 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated quality checks at each step; we can tune thresholds based on your evals.
[09:15] Jordan: ok wrapping into next steps, we'll share cost scenarios and a benchmark plan. any final questions?
[09:25] Lina: what's the expected timeline to get the per-route cost data and the security pack?
[09:30] Sam: per-route spreadsheet by end of this week, security pack by next Tuesday (2026-07-02).
[09:40] Maya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[09:45] Jordan: thanks all — we'll follow up with action items.

Notes (auto): Transcription imperfect in spots (names and acronyms). Customer asked for dedicated sizing, private deployment options, per-route cost breakdown, prefix entropy alerting, and benchmark on p95 latency. Redwood to provide cost scenarios, security pack, and schedule a SE deep dive.

End of transcript.
